market_holds: Spot $100.68 (sealed 18:09 UTC; ~$100.8 at 19:20 UTC on Yahoo 30m bars). Front-expiry (11-13) straddle implies 13.3% with ATM IV 225%. Skew is -27 vol points (25d put IV minus 25d call IV), so calls are dearer than puts: the options market is already paying for upside/squeeze. Put/call OI is 1.32. Two prior prints, both down: 2026-06-23 -19.6% and 2026-08-12 -11.9% (sealed baseline), each after a core beat and a FY raise. The Q1 drop was on the margin guide, the Q2 drop on a GAAP revenue 'miss' ($180.1m against a 'consensus' of $194m, which was really the core guide). Run-in: -29% over 20 days and +23% over 5 days off the 11-05 low of $81.71. That low came with the sector: SMH 447.7 to 501.2 (+12%) and CRWV +29% over the same days, so CBRS moved about 2x SMH and the bounce is mostly tape, not company news. The only company-specific item was the CEO's 11-05 rebuttal of the Culper short report of 10-28 on wafer life. Consensus: Q3 revenue $215.8m and EPS -$0.13 (Earnings Whispers preview of 11-04), which sits at the top of the core guide of $214-216m; the EW whisper is -$0.03. Q4 consensus is $273.2m (Benzinga, via search snippet), which implies FY of about $890m, the top of the FY core guide of $880-890m. FY2027 revenue consensus is $2.96bn (TIKR, 11-07), above management's 'more than triple' floor of about $2.66bn. Analysts cut targets into the print but kept buys (UBS to $250 from $330 on 11-02; average about $262-275). Short interest was about 19.9m shares as of the early-November settlement, up 5.7m (equibles snippet). The IPO lock-up's final release fell at the 180-day mark (about 11-09/11-10), before the print, so locked holders are now free to sell into the reaction. The stock trades on core revenue, the Q4/FY guide (the Q4 implied core is about $264-274m, a +23-27% QoQ step-up), the core gross margin recovery from the Q3 'trough' guide of 38-40%, and whether 2027 is reaffirmed.
view: Management has beaten its own core guide on the one quarter where it gave one ahead of time (Q2: $209.9m against about $194m guided, GM 40.6% against 36-38%). The Q3 guide of $214-216m is only +2-3% QoQ because capacity is the binding constraint, so a core beat to the low/mid $220s is the likely base case. That is largely expected: consensus already sits at the top of the guide and the whisper is well above consensus. The reaction will turn on the Q4/FY guide. A raise that only carries the Q3 beat through to FY leaves the implied Q4 near $264-269m, slightly below the $273m Q4 consensus. A real Q4 raise needs new owned capacity to arrive on time, and the dated public trail on new US sites points to small and late arrivals: the Digi Power X Alabama campus delivers its first 15 MW by December 2026 (single source), Europe's first capacity comes by year end, and Oracle and AWS Bedrock are 2027. The 10-Q shows leases with 2026 commencement dates ($753m and $2.3bn undiscounted signed in Q3), which supports some Q4 capacity. Today a direct peer, Nebius, fell about 17% because third-party colocation deliveries slipped into H1 2027, while CBRS was flat. That read-through is real but weak: CoreWeave beat and raised two days earlier and rose about 25%. A second recurring hazard is mechanical. GAAP revenue is reduced by the OpenAI warrant amortisation ($44.3m in Q2, proportional to OpenAI revenue, so likely larger in Q3), so the headline GAAP revenue (likely below $200m) will again print under a $215.8m 'consensus' set on the core basis. That produced the 'miss' headline in August; the second time the market should see through it faster, and the window runs to the next open. Against all of this, expectations are far lower than at either earlier print: the stock is 62% off its post-Q2 peak at about 13x forward sales, short interest is rising, and sentiment is bearish. A clean beat with a Q4 GM rebound and a reaffirmed 2027 could squeeze hard. A Q4 guide light on capacity timing, or a hedged 2027, could take another 15-20% off. I cannot see which way the Q4 line lands with any confidence, and the options already lean up, so there is no direction worth a recommendation. Slightly below 50, because consensus sits at the top of every range and the stock has sold off both prior prints.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the Q4/FY core guide against a consensus already at the top of the range ($273m Q4, about $890m FY), and it depends on capacity timing that I cannot see in the public record. The evidence on both sides is real: a beat history, a reset valuation and a building short base on one side; a peer's colocation delays today, a recurring GAAP-versus-core headline gap, and a stock that sold off both prior beat-and-raise prints on the other. It does not net to a direction the price lacks, and the option skew already pays for upside.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 core guide clearly above $273m with Q4 core GM back above 43% and a quantified 2027 at or above $2.96bn would make this an up print (likely a squeeze beyond the 13% implied). A FY guide held at $880-890m after a Q3 beat (implied Q4 cut), or any mention of data-center delivery slippage, would make it a down print.

self_critique: The strongest case for long: management sandbagged Q2 by about 8% and called Q3 the margin trough while still guiding only +2-3% QoQ. Consensus is at the guide, not above it; the whisper is far above. The stock trades at a fraction of its earlier multiple with a growing short base, and the same tape just rewarded CoreWeave's beat-and-raise with +25%. A clean print could move 20%+ up. The strongest case for short: consensus sits at the top of every range, and the Q4 step-up needs capacity that peers say is slipping. The GAAP headline will read as a miss again, freshly unlocked holders can sell any bounce, and the stock sold off both previous beat-and-raise prints. Both cases are plausible and I cannot tell which is more likely, which is why there is no recommendation.
approach_notes: P6 helped most: splitting the run-in from the tape showed the +23% bounce is beta, and the peer-print read-throughs (CRWV up, NBIS down) cancelled. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' was hard here because the deciding input, the capacity delivery schedule, has almost no public trail before the release.
